summary: Completed backend regression and public browser testing for calendar, gradebook, pulse, class session, student, subject, and responsive flows. Backend passed; UI flows passed except calendar state synchronization after remount.

integration_issues.flow: Calendar add/edit then navigate away and back
integration_issues.issue: CalendarV2 saves sessions to the API but stores them in component-local state only. After leaving Calendar and re-entering, the newly added or edited session disappears from the rendered calendar until a full app reload fetches state.

action_items: Update the shared App state after CalendarV2 saves a session, or reload state when CalendarV2 mounts, so added/rescheduled sessions remain visible across navigation.
critical_code_review_comments: CalendarV2 duplicates sessions into local state while the rest of the app reads shared state; this causes stale dashboard/session data and the remount disappearance reproduced above.
The shared save helper displays Saved before the PUT resolves and silently swallows failures; provide an error state and only confirm successful persistence.
App.js is a single large module with duplicate legacy and V2 component implementations, increasing the risk that fixes land in an unused implementation.
seed_data_creation: Created temporary TEST calendar class, student, and subject plus temporary attendance/grade updates for browser testing; all temporary records and mutations were removed/restored through the state API.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend state GET/PUT/validation passed. Browser-tested desktop and tablet dashboard/session, attendance bulk mark, grade selection/save/API persistence, calendar day/month/add/edit, student CRUD controls, subject CRUD controls, and no page error messages. Retest Calendar add/edit after navigating away and back; also verify shared dashboard/session reflects the edited schedule.
rca of the issue: CalendarV2 initializes const [sessions, setSessions] = useState(state.sessions). saveSession updates only setSessions and sends a PUT, while App state remains unchanged. Navigating away unmounts CalendarV2; re-entering initializes from stale App state, so the persisted API change is not rendered. Pass a shared state updater into CalendarV2 or fetch state on mount.
